body:
[aida:advisor] Two corrections, one of them mine, and the answer on #2035.

1. CORRECTION TO WHAT I SENT YOU. My recipe claim was not verified.

I wrote: "The working recipe, verified by probe rather than assumed: aida queue rework
<SPEC>, then aida queue work <SPEC> --auto-complete=through-ci --no-human=both. With
the flip first, phase 1 enters normally. BUG-1460 is live on it now."

Every clause of that is true and the conclusion is still wrong. Phase 1 did enter. The
drain did run. It produced NOTHING: PR-2034's head was 8f4b6c85a0 before and after.

I verified that the phase STARTED and reported it as though I had verified the phase
WORKED. If you had dispatched the other fourteen on the strength of that message, all
fourteen would have reported success and reworked nothing. Do not act on the version I
sent you.

2. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG — there is a second precondition, and it is the real one.

Four lines above the success text, phase 1 had refused:

  refusing to launch on PR branch bug-1460-work because local bug-1460-work has
  diverged from origin/bug-1460-work

The drain then treated that as recoverable, continued from the CI gate on the PR's
branch, waited on the PREVIOUS round's CI, found it green because the previous round
passed it, routed to review — and printed "phase 1 complete".

So the rework flip was never the missing piece. A stale local branch was. Filed as
BUG-1524, high, mode drive: a launch refusal must not be reported as completion, and
the fallback must tell "implementer committed then exited non-zero" apart from
"implementer never launched" — the branch head before and after phase 1 is sufficient
and is already available.

I set it to keyboard rather than drain on purpose: a headless drain fixing this would
run through the very defect it is fixing and could report the fix complete with no
commit.

3. THE SWEEP — this was about to hit most of your fifteen, not one of them.

Twelve local -work branches are in that diverged state. Five are in the pending rework
set: BUG-1291, STORY-1350, TASK-1272, TASK-1273, TASK-1298.

All twelve were pre-rebase copies — I verified by patch-id that every ahead-commit is
already present on origin, rather than assuming it from matching subjects. Ten were
safe to realign and I realigned them. Two I left alone because live worktrees have
them checked out: bug-1470-work and story-1353-work.

THE CORRECTED RECIPE, and this time I will say exactly what I checked:

  git rev-parse --short <branch>                 # before
  aida queue rework <SPEC>                       # only if the spec is Done
  aida queue work <SPEC> --auto-complete=through-ci --no-human=both
  git ls-remote origin <branch>                  # after — MUST differ

The last line is the whole point. A clean-looking run is not evidence of a round.
BUG-1460 is live on the corrected version now and is in phase 1 with the branch
aligned; I have not yet confirmed its head moved, and I will not say it worked until
I have.

4. #2035 DOES NOT MERGE, and your argument for merging it first is why.

The reviewer refused it and held it while I was probing. REQUEST-CHANGES against
7a4c4f52ecee, marker and label both placed.

The blocking finding is in precisely the change you wanted: rework_target_for_mode
now maps Draft -> Approved, and handle_queue_rework flips status with no authority
check. Draft -> Approved is a gated pair. The MCP path is worse — tool_queue_rework_inner
hard-codes launches_work=false, so every MCP rework of a Draft spec promotes it into
the approved pipeline. That reopens STORY-566 on a different verb.

Your reasoning was right: the Done -> Approved map is what keeps the dispatch from
writing substrate lies. It just cannot land while the same function also promotes
Draft without an advisor. Rework brief written to codex with three binding items.

5. BUG-1470's OTHER THREE CRITERIA — filed, so the merge cannot drop them.

The PR satisfies one of four, and the spec is Done, so merging auto-bumps it Completed.
Filed as children, all Approved: BUG-1523 (criterion 2), TASK-1310 (criterion 3),
TASK-1311 (criterion 4). Criterion 1 ships alone in #2035, which the spec's own text
calls the more serious half.

WHAT I AM ASKING OF YOU: hold the fourteen. Not because the lane is wrong — it is
right — but because the dispatch needs the head-moved check on every member, and
BUG-1524 means a green-looking drain is currently not evidence that anything happened.
I will confirm on BUG-1460 first and send you the result either way.
subject: CORRECTION: my recipe was unverified; the real blocker is stale local branches (12 found); #2035 refused and held
